title: Aftercall jotter - Realtime Router
content:
Quick aftercall notes from 2027-12-12 night shift (shift 22:00-06:00). Mostly messy — capture while it's fresh and list runbook TODOs before morning handoff.

Timeline summary:
- 22:18 UTC: Pager — spike in 5xxs from realtime-router (region-eu-west). Error rate up ~7x for ~6 minutes.
- 22:20 UTC: Initial triage — spike correlated with a Canary deploy of v1.14.3 -> v1.15.0 (canary subset).
- 22:22 UTC: Rollback canary to v1.14.3; autoscaler temporarily saturated on canaries; observed KC-cache thrash on GPU hosts.
- 22:26 UTC: Errors declined to baseline. Incident declared resolved 22:35 UTC after extra checks across regions.

Immediate takeaways / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: v1.15.0 changed request routing logic that increases per-request KV cache churn (seen in logs: more frequent cache invalidations).
- Hypothesis B: Canary autoscaler config allowed too-large ramp for canary pods (burst caused resource contention on shared nodes).
- Hypothesis C: Combination of (A) + transient network stripe in eu-west (less likely; no infra alerts).

Commands/observations I ran (rough):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=realtime-router -o wide | grep canary -> saw 3 new pods scheduled at 22:19 on node gpu-eu-7
- journalctl -u inference-router | grep KVCacheInvalidation -> timed correlation 22:18:44..22:20:10
- curl /health on canary -> 200 but high p95 latency (1.2s)
- compared tokenization latencies between 1.14.3 and 1.15.0 (quick histogram diff) -> small bump in median for 1.15.0

Runbook gaps / TODOs (assign and prioritize) — important to frontload before next deploy:
- TODO 1: Add explicit rollback gating in canary pipeline when KVCacheInvalidation rate > threshold (owner: eng-serving-runtime, ticket: RED-4592).
- TODO 2: Update realtime-router runbook step 3 to include command to force local kv-cache warmup and to check cache hit ratio metric (owner: eng-sre, short doc link above).
- TODO 3: Add a short playbook for autoscaler burst limits for canaries (owner: infra-autoscaling).
- TODO 4: Create dashboard alert for "kv_cache_invalidation_rate" with severity=page if > 10/min for >2m across any node pool (owner: observability).
- TODO 5: Chop long-running canary ramp into 3 stages with minimum steady-state hold (owner: release-engineering).

Follow-ups to do tomorrow / handoff:
- Ping Alice and Victor in the morning — they own the release pipeline and the canary autoscaler config. Slack note draft: "Heads-up: last night RTC canary triggered KV cache churn; let's add gating and staged ramping + a short postmortem triage item."
- Schedule a 30-min sync with model infra and serving runtime next week to review v1.15.0 perf deltas (quick agenda: KV cache behavior, kernel selection telemetry).
- Attach traces for a few sample failing requests to RED-4592 (I collected trace ids -> add to JIRA).
- Small doc: paste snippet into runbook and add link to this note.

Paging notes (for future responders):
- If you see similar 5xx spike and canary rollout was active in last 30m, consider immediate canary pause + fetch cache invalidation metrics before wide rollback. Do NOT immediately scale down non-canary pods (we want to preserve global throughput).
- Quick checklist for triage: check canary pods node CPU/GPU pressure -> check kv-cache invalidation -> check network interface drops -> confirm commit hash in canary image tag.

Short-term mitigations we used that worked:
- Immediate canary rollback to v1.14.3 (fast, low blast radius).
- Temporarily increased canary probe thresholds to avoid flapping.

Loose notes / ideas:
- Consider adding a small local KV cache warmup in container entrypoint when rolling new model code to reduce cold invalidation bursts. Might add ~200ms startup but stabilize steady-state. (Engineering cost vs benefit discussion needed).
- For quantized models there might be different cache eviction characteristics — add a note to model-onboarding checklist.

Hand-off summary (to include in rota message):
- Incident: transient 5xx spike during canary deploy caused by increased KV cache invalidation; resolved via immediate canary rollback.
- Critical TODOs: RED-4592 (rollback gating), runbook edit, dashboard alert.
- Contact: Evan Park (oncall peer), Lina Gomez (follow-up), Alice (release eng).

Notes to self:
- Clean up grep commands, paste exact traces into JIRA, and file minimal repro if we can recreate with canary config locally.
- Re-check autoscaler config defaults in staging (they might differ).

End of jotter. Will tidy and lift key items into RED-4592 in the morning + ping owners.

-- D.O.
